memory_candidates.content: Bash `read` silently drops a trailing empty field when splitting delimited text: `IFS=: read -r a b <<< "4:foo:"` yields b="foo" not "foo:" -- the trailing colon and everything after it vanishes. This corrupts any line-parsing loop over `grep -n` output where the matched content can itself end in the delimiter (e.g. a `// CONFIRM:` marker with an empty payload). Fix: use `IFS= read -r rawline` (no field splitting) then extract fields manually via `lnum="${rawline%%:*}"` / `content="${rawline#*:}"`, which preserves trailing delimiters exactly.

When adding a second mechanical checker to an extension that already has one (e.g. typst-element-lint.sh -> chapter-quality-check.sh), delegate shared territory to the existing script rather than re-implementing it, and grep-verify the delegation held (e.g. `grep -nE '<element-name-list>' new-checker.sh` should return only header prose, never matching logic). Also watch for an unrelated rule in the new checker reusing the same name list for its own heuristic (e.g. counting semantic-element invocations as 'claims') -- that collides with the delegation-verification grep even though it isn't a second placement implementation, and is worth simplifying away to keep the grep's signal clean.
